Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: gameplay concept screenshot for a Korean folklore game planning article.
Primary request: an opaque 16:9 landscape image of crisp 2D pixel art gameplay, a playable top-down simultaneous turn strategy puzzle called "Moving Mountain". Show the actual game board clearly, not a poster or title screen.
Scene/backdrop: sunny Korean village meadow with small tiled-roof homes and a turquoise stream on the right, a little safe wooden bridge exit at the right edge.
Subject and rules visualized: a strict top-down 8 by 8 square tile board occupies the central 75 percent of the screen. A cute leafy walking mountain is a compact 2 by 2 tile creature near the center, with a smiling rock face, little feet, leafy pine crown, ochre stone and green foliage. There are exactly three distinct hanbok-wearing village characters on the board: two lookout characters each project an unmistakable straight rectangular yellow gaze cone along a row or column toward the mountain. The two gaze cones terminate on the mountain and show small eye pictograms to indicate observation freezes it. The third character is a guide with a small handcart, planning a path to the wooden bridge. Blue highlighted projected move tiles trace a short safe path for the cart. Orange outlined footprints mark two future dangerous mountain tiles. Blue direction arrows around each character indicate orientation matters. Show the mountain frozen this turn because two villagers look at it.
HUD: compact cream pixel HUD across top with only "TURN 07" and "PLAN"; a miniature simultaneous plan timeline at bottom containing exactly three large action icons in sequence (eye, turn arrow, cart), labeled "1", "2", "3"; a small eye indicator over the mountain. Keep the visual board uncluttered and understandable. No cards.
Style/medium: authentic hand-crafted 16-bit 2D pixel art with deliberate visible square pixels, hard clean sprite edges, clear silhouettes, limited vivid teal, leaf green, ochre, cream palette. Direct overhead camera, no isometric perspective, no 3D. Bright playful adventurous mood. Short English labels and numerals only, no title, no watermark. Image should communicate the playable decision of who observes the mountain and who moves while everyone resolves together. Render full finished 16:9 landscape gameplay scene.
visual_qa: Two yellow observation lanes, three village characters, blue cart path, orange danger footprints and three-step action timeline are visible.
Generated board has 9 columns and 8 rows rather than the requested 8x8; tile counts in the written rules are authoritative.
Mountain occupies roughly two-by-two visual cells; exact collision bounds require the prototype.

images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: gameplay concept screenshot for a Korean folklore game planning article.
Primary request: opaque 16:9 landscape crisp 2D pixel art gameplay screenshot of a top-down action roguelite about a young Korean smith girl and her cute baby iron-eating Bulgasari companion. This is a playable action screen, not a poster or title screen.
Scene/backdrop: sunny forest smithy courtyard in Korean folklore countryside, leafy bamboo walls, a little tile-roof forge, stone path, teal stream edge and scrap metal piles. Entire world is direct overhead 2D tile-and-sprite game art.
Gameplay: the hanbok-wearing young smith girl with a small hammer is actively kiting exactly three mischievous wooden training constructs toward two visible rust-colored iron scrap piles. A pale translucent dodge afterimage of the girl and a short curved dashed motion trail show a dodge in progress. Beside her, a medium-sized chunky Bulgasari companion with glowing ochre iron armor plates, a playful elephant-like short snout and broad paws is visibly chewing a piece of metal; small square metallic crumbs. Tiny damage-free impact sparks on wooden constructs show friendly sparring rather than violence. The companion should be obviously bulkier than the girl and still cute.
Critical route decision: at right side show a clearly narrow bamboo gate shortcut, with a small white outlined large-companion silhouette and crossed-circle pictogram at the gate to indicate the largest form cannot fit. A second wider route goes around the bamboo gate through a wooden barricade that can be broken by the large armored form. Use simple cyan path arrows to distinguish narrow shortcut and wide breakable route, while remaining an actual in-game screenshot.
HUD: compact pixel HUD top left with three red heart pictograms and a belly gauge labeled "IRON 4/6" consisting of six square slots, exactly four filled ochre. Top right HUD has three clearly different companion silhouette size tiers (small, medium, large) with the medium tier highlighted. Bottom center shows three tool cooldown pictograms: hammer "2", iron scrap "1", dodge boot "0". Text only these short English labels and numerals, no title, no watermark.
Style/medium: authentic 16-bit hand-crafted 2D pixel art, crisp visible square pixels and hard sprite edges, no smooth vectors or 3D. Readable characters separated from terrain. Bright teal, leaf-green, ochre, warm cream and rust palette. Sunny playful comedy, no killing, no gore, no dark horror. Gameplay decision is what metal to feed the companion, which changes size, protection and accessible paths. Finished 16:9 screenshot composition with gameplay occupying most of image.
visual_qa: Smith girl, dodge afterimage, three wooden training constructs, iron scrap piles and metal-eating companion are visible.
Edited IRON 3/6 HUD shows three filled cells and three empty cells; three size silhouettes retain medium highlighted, matching article rules.
Narrow bamboo path has a largest-size blocked pictogram, and wider route is shown around a wooden barricade.
Action scene uses a slightly elevated top-down RPG view.
Targeted image edit corrected the gauge; scene layout, characters, dodge ghost, routes and tool cooldowns remain visually consistent.
